note: First-party OWASP Benchmark v1.2 result for Zennoxa Shield. Shield-only — contains no competitor data.

tool.name: Zennoxa Shield
tool.engine: SAST: single-line rules plus data-flow tracking (collections, constant branches, helper functions, calls into other classes of the project, encoders per output context, algorithm names read from .properties files)
tool.release_note: Measured with the public CLI release v0.8.0 (shield-linux-amd64) on 2026-11-16. v0.7.0 scored +0.582 (precision 92.5%, recall 63.7%, FPR 5.5%) on both scan targets.

benchmark.score_metric: Benchmark Score = True Positive Rate − False Positive Rate (Youden's J), strict OWASP CWE-per-category match; higher is better

testcode_folder_only.why_it_differs: 124 vulnerable cases depend on helper classes and on benchmark.properties, which live outside that folder

caveat: A perfect score on a public suite means the engine models the code shapes that suite is built from. It is not a claim about other code: on NIST Juliet for Java (nine injection weaknesses, 5,772 cases), which was not used during development, the data-flow findings of v0.8.0 catch 51.9% of the vulnerable cases and flag none of the fixed variants.
reproduce: Install the Shield CLI v0.8.0 and verify the download against SHA256SUMS on the release.
shield scan BenchmarkJava --format json --output findings.json   (for the second figure: shield scan BenchmarkJava/src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode ...)
Score findings.json against BenchmarkJava/expectedresults-1.2.csv: a finding counts for a test case when it is reported in that case's file with the CWE the suite expects for it.
The score depends on the Shield release; this result is from v0.8.0, measured 2026-11-16.
reproducibility_note: Every figure here is produced on the public OWASP Benchmark v1.2 suite (2,740 labelled Java cases). To compare other tools, use OWASP's own published scorecards; run every tool at its default configuration.
